identity.title: AffectGPT: A New Dataset, Model, and Benchmark for Emotion Understanding with Multimodal Large Language Models

problem.claim: Advance multimodal emotion recognition toward complex emotion understanding with video-based and natural-language outputs.

gap.claim: Existing work lacks large-scale descriptive emotion annotations and a multimodal-centric framework for maximizing MLLMs in emotion understanding.

contributions.claim: MER-Caption, described as the largest descriptive emotion dataset to date, contains over 2K fine-grained emotion categories across 115K samples and is constructed through model-based crowdsourcing.
AffectGPT uses pre-fusion operations designed to improve multimodal integration.
MER-UniBench unifies evaluation for typical MER tasks and MLLM-style free-form natural-language outputs, with tailored metrics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a combined new dataset, model, and unified benchmark for MLLM-based emotion understanding.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AffectGPT performs robustly across various MER tasks in extensive experiments.
The authors report releasing the code and dataset to support further emotion-understanding research and development.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLMs expand MER from discriminative recognition toward complex understanding with video abilities and natural-language description.
The field is reported to lack large-scale intensive descriptive annotations and a multimodal-focused framework.
The paper establishes a benchmark comprising MER-Caption and AffectGPT, then adds MER-UniBench for unified task evaluation.
The authors report robust AffectGPT performance across various MER tasks and release the code and dataset.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns three linked artifacts—a dataset, a model, and a benchmark—with the stated annotation, integration, and evaluation gaps.

lessons.interpretation: Bundling complementary resources can make a research agenda easier to evaluate and extend.
lessons.application: When addressing a capability gap, pair the proposed method with task-relevant data and evaluation that matches its output form.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when the task already has adequate data and evaluation infrastructure, or when adding artifacts would obscure a narrowly scoped contribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the comparison systems, task-by-task metrics, or what “robust performance” quantitatively means.
The basis and scope of the “largest ... to date” dataset claim are not detailed.
The abstract does not report ablations isolating the effect of pre-fusion operations or the crowdsourcing strategy.
